title: Journey - Walking Through Grief - Day 4: A future and a hope

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Walking Through Grief. <short pause> This is day four, A Future and a Hope. <short pause> It's the last day of this journey, though not the end of your grief. <short pause> Nobody is asking you to be finished. <short pause> We'll only lift our eyes a little way along the road.

The prophet Jeremiah once wrote to people who had lost their home, and the life they knew. <short pause> He didn't tell them it would soon be over. <short pause> It would be seventy years. <short pause> He told them to build houses there, to plant gardens, and to eat. <short pause> And in that same letter, chapter twenty-nine, verse eleven, he gave them these words from God.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

parts.style: tender, soft, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: It was a promise made to grieving people, far from what they loved. <short pause> It doesn't explain your loss, or call it good. <short pause> It says that God's thoughts toward you are still peace. <short pause> You can miss them all your life... <short pause> and still be led into a life.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: A garden begins very small. <short pause> Is there one seed you could plant, without leaving them behind? <short pause> A walk. A recipe of theirs. A day marked kindly on the calendar. <short pause> If it's too soon, leave the seed in His hand. <short pause> It will keep.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Lord, I can't see very far. <short pause> Take my love, and my sorrow, and the days I don't know how to live. <short pause> Give me enough light for the next step. <short pause> Lead me on. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: Here are your four prayers for the road. <short pause> Walk with me. <short pause> Remember with me. <short pause> Comfort me. <short pause> Lead me on. <short pause> Come back to any of these days, in any order, whenever you need them. <short pause> You do not walk alone.
